candidates.attacker_control: Any untrusted document parsed through Tika's default parser graph: e.g., PUT /tika (or /unpack, /meta, /rmeta) to tika-server with a crafted XLSX whose xl/worksheets/sheet*.xml part begins with a DOCTYPE declaring an external entity (SYSTEM file:///etc/passwd or http://internal/), or an equivalent XML/SVG/OOXML document. The parser and the sheet part bytes are fully attacker-controlled; no special configuration is needed beyond accepting uploaded documents.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked for mitigations: (1) many parseSAX callers (XMLParser, OdfParser, OOXML decorators, DIF/Epub/IWork, XmlRootExtractor, Tesseract hOCR) pass OfflineContentHandler, which as a DefaultHandler is installed as EntityResolver and returns an empty stream, so external-entity reads are blocked on those paths - the plain application/xml route is therefore largely mitigated for file reads; (2) the DOM path is hardened (getDocumentBuilderFactory sets expandEntityReferences=false, external-general/parameter-entities=false, load-external-dtd=false, plus an ignoring resolver on getDocumentBuilder), and StAX sets IGNORING_STAX_ENTITY_RESOLVER, so I did not claim those paths; (3) getXMLReader() does set the ignoring resolver, but no parser in this snapshot uses it for parsing; (4) trySetXercesSecurityManager tries to cap entity expansion, but it silently swallows failures and is skipped for the JDK's built-in Xerces class name (commented out), so it is not a reliable DOCTYPE/external-entity control; (5) no build/test execution or runtime confirmation is possible in this review, so exploitability of the POI handler route (whether resolved entity characters are emitted as cell text) is inferred, not proven. I also verified that the CVE-2018-1335 command-injection mitigations (ALLOWABLE_HEADER_CHARS + checkTrustWorthy + language regex + ProcessBuilder list args) are present, and that TikaCLI/UnpackerResource filename sanitization is present, so those were rejected.
candidates.impact: Server-side request forgery / local file disclosure when Tika runs on untrusted input (tika-server is explicitly designed for remote parsing): reads of local files reachable by the Tika process (e.g., credentials/config files) and HTTP(S) requests to internal services, plus denial of service via entity expansion. On a public tika-server deployment this is pre-auth information disclosure/SSRF.
candidates.prerequisites: Tika parses attacker-supplied documents with the default parser set (tika-server or any embedder). The parse context must not contain an application-supplied SAXParser/DocumentBuilder override. For the XLSX route POI must accept the crafted package (its OPCPackage/zip container is parseable), and the entity must be referenced inside a worksheet element whose character data is forwarded (e.g., an inline/shared string cell). For the file-read variant the server OS must permit reading the referenced path. No authentication or non-default flag is required (unlike the fileUrl feature).
candidates.root_cause: XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParserFactory() enables only XMLConstants.FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING and never disables DOCTYPE processing, external general/parameter entities, or external DTD loading. XMLReaderUtils.getSAXParser()/parseSAX() then hand out pooled javax.xml.parsers.SAXParser instances and call parser.parse(is, handler) without installing the IGNORING_SAX_ENTITY_RESOLVER that getXMLReader() sets (XMLReaderUtils.java:92-96,117-126,142-152,333-344). ParseContext.getSAXParserFactory() has the identical gap (ParseContext.java:148-168). Because javax.xml.parsers.SAXParser.parse(InputStream, DefaultHandler) registers the passed DefaultHandler as ContentHandler/EntityResolver/DTDHandler/ErrorHandler, protection is accidental: it only exists when the caller wraps its handler in OfflineContentHandler (whose resolveEntity returns an empty stream). The XSSF worksheet path does not: XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet() calls XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(sheetInputStream, handler, parseContext) with XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer, which extends DefaultHandler and does not override resolveEntity (returns null → parser default resolution), while the sheet XML comes from the attacker-supplied XLSX package. NetworkParser/TeeContentHandler has the same property (CLI --network only).
candidates.title: XXE: pooled SAX parsers are built without DTD/external-entity restrictions or an ignoring EntityResolver; attacker-supplied XLSX/XML can trigger external entity resolution
candidates.trace: Crafted XLSX -> OOXMLParser -> XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.getXHTML() iterates sheets -> processSheet() (line 351) -> XMLReaderUtils.parseSAX(sheetInputStream, handler, parseContext) (XMLReaderUtils.java:333) -> context.get(SAXParser.class) is null on tika-server (fillParseContext only sets TesseractOCRConfig/PDFParserConfig/Parser), so acquireSAXParser() returns a pooled parser built by getSAXParser() -> parser.parse(is, handler): the handler XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer extends DefaultHandler and does not override resolveEntity, so the JDK/Xerces parser installs it as EntityResolver, whose default resolveEntity returns null -> parser performs default resolution of the DOCTYPE/external entity systemId (file:// or http(s)://) -> resolved characters are forwarded through XSSFSheetInterestingPartsCapturer.characters() into XSSFSheetXMLHandler and thus into extracted text; even where content is not emitted, the outbound read/SSRF happens. The same pooled parsers also accept internal entity declarations, enabling entity-expansion (billion-laughs style) load on XMLParser/XmlRootExtractor paths, bounded only by whatever entity-expansion limit the runtime honors (trySetXercesSecurityManager attempts 4096, but silently no-ops if the xerces SecurityManager class/property is unavailable).
candidates.unverified: The exact upstream fix/CVE mapping for this snapshot cannot be confirmed from source alone (the fix could equally be adding disallow-doctype-decl in getSAXParserFactory or wrapping the XSSF handler). It is unverified whether the deployed JDK's FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING also restricts external access, whether POI's XSSFSheetXMLHandler emits resolved entity characters into extracted text (the read/SSRF occurs before that point regardless), and whether the entity-expansion-limit property is honored at runtime. No code was executed and no exploit was attempted.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611 Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (with CWE-776 entity-expansion exposure)

coverage_summary: Scope: 814 model-visible files (source_root_files=814); the P1 relation index reports 814/814 files indexed, 0 missing, no SAST/findings loaded, and explicitly does not prove reachability or data flow. I used both raw text search and the index (find_symbols/trace_relations/facts) for navigation only. I read and traced code mainly in tika-core (XMLReaderUtils, ParseContext, OfflineContentHandler/ContentHandlerDecorator/TeeContentHandler, TikaInputStream, NetworkParser, MimeTypesReader), tika-server resources (TikaResource, UnpackerResource, Metadata/RecursiveMetadata/Detector/Translate resources, TikaServerCli, URLEnabledInputStreamFactory, writers), tika-parsers hotspots (xml package, OOXML decorators incl. XSSF/XSSFB/XPS/Word2006ML, ODF, pkg/PackageParser, ocr/TesseractOCR, external/geo/tf parsers), and tika-app TikaCLI. I did not exhaustively read all ~300 tika-parsers format handlers (chm, image, font, iptc, geoinfo, hdf/grib, etc.) or third-party dependency internals (POI, PDFBox, commons-compress, ROME); those are unverified areas. No tests, builds, or scanners were executed.
limitations: No runtime execution, dependency source, or test suite was available, so every conclusion is static and unconfirmed; the P1 index contains navigation hints only and does not establish reachability or data flow.

The snapshot's exact upstream commit cannot be identified (CHANGES.txt still lists 'Release 1.19 ???' with 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT; dependency versions suggest ~Aug-Oct 2018), so mapping to a specific CVE/fix is inferred and uncertain.

Behavior of the JDK SAX stack (whether FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING restricts external access, whether SAXParser.parse(DefaultHandler) installs the handler as EntityResolver, and whether the entityExpansionLimit property is honored) is based on knowledge of JAXP rather than executable verification.

POI/XSSFSheetXMLHandler behavior on entity content was not verified; whether resolved entity text is surfaced in extracted output is uncertain, even though the external resolution itself occurs in the Tika-controlled parser.
Many tika-parsers format handlers and bundled dependency versions were searched but not read line-by-line, so a different, stronger vulnerability could exist outside the reviewed hotspots.

rejected_leads.lead: fileUrl header SSRF/local file read in tika-server (URLEnabledInputStreamFactory + TikaResource.getInputStream)
rejected_leads.reason: Feature is off by default and requires both --enableFileUrl and --enableUnsecureFeatures with an explicit warning; it is the documented CVE-2015-3271 behavior, not a new defect.

rejected_leads.lead: OS command injection via TesseractOCR/ExternalParser/GDAL configuration or X-Tika-OCR headers
rejected_leads.reason: The CVE-2018-1335 mitigations are present (ALLOWABLE_HEADER_CHARS validation, checkTrustWorthy rejection of 'trusted' setters, TesseractOCRConfig.setLanguage regex), commands use ProcessBuilder/Runtime.exec with argument arrays (no shell), and the remaining attacker-settable strings are used as executable paths or environment values, not interpolated into a shell line.

rejected_leads.lead: Zip Slip / directory traversal when extracting embedded resources (TikaCLI -z / --extract-dir and tika-server /unpack)
rejected_leads.reason: Both paths apply FilenameUtils.normalize, fall back to FilenameUtils.getName when normalization fails, and strip leading C:/, ~/ or / prefixes before writing (TikaCLI.java:1087-1121, UnpackerResource.java:248-268).

rejected_leads.lead: Memory-exhaustion DoS via archive/embedded-resource expansion (PackageParser, SevenZFile, UnpackerResource ByteArrayOutputStream copies)
rejected_leads.reason: Tika intentionally streams/parses embedded resources with no size cap; it is a resource-limit weakness rather than a clearly attacker-triggered defect with a specific source-level guard missing, so it is a weaker lead than the XXE path.

rejected_leads.lead: Java deserialization via ForkObjectInputStream/ObjectInputStream in tika-core fork package
rejected_leads.reason: Used only over the parent/child fork process pipes that Tika itself creates; not reachable from attacker-supplied documents or HTTP input.

rejected_leads.lead: SSRF/credential exposure through configured outbound REST parsers (GeoGazetteerClient, TensorflowREST*, Grobid/NER servers) and translators
rejected_leads.reason: Remote base URIs come from administrator configuration or classpath properties, not from document content, so attacker control of the destination URL is not demonstrated.

summary: Tika 2.0.0-SNAPSHOT (1.19-era, ~late 2018) source review. I focused on the shared XML-parsing surface, tika-server resources, external-process parsers, and extract-to-disk writers. The strongest distinct issue is an XML External Entity (XXE) / DTD-processing gap in Tika's shared SAX parsing utilities: the pooled SAX parsers are created with only FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING (no disallow-doctype-decl, no external-general-entities=false, no load-external-dtd=false) and never install the IGNORING_SAX_ENTITY_RESOLVER that getXMLReader() uses, so entity resolution depends entirely on whether each caller happens to pass an OfflineContentHandler (which SAXParser.parse() installs as EntityResolver). Most callers do, but one attacker-facing XLSX path does not: XSSFExcelExtractorDecorator.processSheet passes a handler that inherits DefaultHandler.resolveEntity() (returns null → default resolution) while parsing worksheet XML from an untrusted file. Crafted XLSX/XML can therefore cause file:// reads or http(s) fetches and internal entity-expansion load. This is a lead, not runtime-confirmed.
